slides.narration: Welcome to Book II, Chapter 7: Designing Natural Types with Operator Overloading. This deck follows the Chapter 1 Slides model: concept on the left, code or evidence on the right, and presenter notes that tell the instructor what to say and do. Modern C++ is not about using the newest syntax because it looks impressive. It is about encoding ownership, lifetime, invariants, generic behavior, and failure boundaries so the program is easier to reason about and harder to misuse.

slides.title: 7.1 Overloading Arithmetic and Comparison Operators
keyPoints: An overloaded operator is a function selected through operator syntax.
It cannot invent a new operator symbol or change the language’s precedence rules.
Its meaning should remain close enough to the conventional operation that a reader can reason about an expression.
For value arithmetic, avoid mutating operands unexpectedly and define how out-of-domain results are reported.
slides.narration: In Book II, Chapter 7, treat 7.1 Overloading Arithmetic and Comparison Operators as a design decision with costs and evidence. An overloaded operator is a function selected through operator syntax. It cannot invent a new operator symbol or change the language’s precedence rules. Its meaning should remain close enough to the conventional operation that a reader can reason about an expression without opening every definition. For value arithmetic, avoid mutating operands unexpectedly and define how out-of-domain results are reported. slides.narration: In Book II, Chapter 7, treat 7.1.2 Defining Meaningful Comparisons as a design decision with costs and evidence. The defaulted three-way comparison compares the quantity’s value representation and supplies a coherent ordering for this type. Equality is consistent with that value model: two quantities with the same accepted integer are equal. Do not default comparison blindly for a type containing caches, raw ownership addresses, or fields that are not part of its logical value. Memberwise ordering is only appropriate when member order expresses the intended semantics. Floating-point types can also have partial-order concerns such as NaN, unlike this bounded integer model. Define the ordering relation required by algorithms and containers before selecting an implementation. Extraction begins with a known value, accepts twelve, then rejects one million and one while preserving twelve. Finally insertion produces the exact string 12. A comparison could be correct while output changes the caller’s formatting state unexpectedly. Avoid one large expression that obscures which operation failed. slides.narration: In Book II, Chapter 7, treat Evidence and interpretation as a design decision with costs and evidence. Two plus three becomes five, and two compares less than three. One million plus one throws because the resulting quantity is outside its domain. The valid input twelve replaces the previous value seven. Reading one million one sets the input stream’s failure state while the object retains twelve. The output stream then produces the exact text 12. This check verifies the formatting contract without forcing line termination into the operator. The failed extraction check verifies both the stream state and preserved object state; checking only one would miss part of the interface. slides.title: Failure clinic — A correct constructor after an invalid addition
keyPoints: A developer writes a constructor that checks a range and assumes every expression returning that type is now safe.
The addition operator performs signed addition before invoking the constructor.
For unrestricted operands, overflow can happen before any range validation runs.
The constructor protects the object state only after it receives a valid representable candidate; it cannot make.
slides.narration: In Book II, Chapter 7, treat Failure clinic — A correct constructor after an invalid addition as a design decision with costs and evidence. A developer writes a constructor that checks a range and assumes every expression returning that type is now safe. The addition operator performs signed addition before invoking the constructor. For unrestricted operands, overflow can happen before any range validation runs. The constructor protects the object state only after it receives a valid representable candidate; it cannot make an earlier undefined operation well-defined. A second defect assigns an extracted candidate directly into the object and validates afterward. As in Chapter 2, a thrown exception or failed stream state does not automatically roll back that assignment. The correction is candidate-first parsing and a visible commit. A graduate-level explanation should say what the abstraction buys, what rule keeps it honest, and what artifact proves the rule: source code, compiler acceptance or rejection, stdout, stderr, exit status, object state, or a test witness.

slides.narration: In Book II, Chapter 7, treat Review answers and solution notes as a design decision with costs and evidence. A failed extraction should preserve the previous value and leave the stream in a failure state. A successful numeric prefix can leave trailing text, which the enclosing parser must validate when whole-input consumption is required. A cache normally should not define logical equality merely because it is a member. Bounded domain validation must happen before committing a value, while machine arithmetic overflow must be prevented before the arithmetic expression is evaluated. Operators should preserve conventional expectations and the type’s invariant together.
